translation_notes: Context shim (_shim.py) stands in for `import bald` (isUrl, getBasename, and a schemaOrg.distribution(container, graph, baseuri) that returns its graph unchanged): the real bald.schemaOrg in this checkout (lib/bald/__init__.py:1463) does not expose a 3-argument distribution() -- a pre-existing mismatch in the source repository, unrelated to the translation. bald2schemaorg_mappings.json is copied verbatim from nc2rdf/ since original.py opens it by relative path.

The one local `so = Namespace("http://schema.org/")` (namespace_ctor) becomes `@prefix so: <http://schema.org/> .`; its single use `so.Dataset` (namespace_term) becomes `so:Dataset`. Not bound `as so` since the object itself is never used, only the prefix.

The four schema_g.add((...)) calls (triple_add) become `+{ }` under a single `@graph schema_g` for the function: add_isolated is the more specific construction here even though the region is drawn from the ns_def_local stratum, per the instruction to always credit the most specific construction. Each add stayed a separate +{ } (no `;` merging) since they are independent statements, some conditional, some inside a loop -- merging would be the DELETE-WHERE-style join pitfall's write-side analogue and would change which triples get added when a branch is skipped.

The static `URIRef("http://schema.org/url")` became the IRI literal `<http://schema.org/url>`; the two runtime-built `URIRef("http://schema.org/" + mapping_idx[currField])` were left as URIRef(...) rather than rewritten to f<...{expr}...>, matching the instruction to translate only the ns_def_local idiom itself (no unrequested refactor of unrelated term construction).

driver.py builds an input graph inline (bald:Container with a plain field, a comma-separated 'keywords' field including a blank entry, and one unmapped predicate that must not appear in the output) since the oracle is isomorphism on the function's *return* value, not a read of a pre-existing fixture file.

`@graph schema_g` lie `so` sur le graphe retourné, que le dépôt sérialise : `so:Dataset` au lieu de `<http://schema.org/Dataset>`. Mêmes triplets, autre écriture : c'est la règle de l'étude (fiche ldpy/027, décision du 2026-10-30), une liaison en plus n'est pas une différence de sens. Le pilote exige que les liaisons de l'original soient conservées, pas que le texte sérialisé soit identique.

validation.method: entry:baldgraph2schemaorg (custom: isomorphism, bindings of the original kept)

repair.driver: pilote réécrit à la main (run_pair ne compare que l'isomorphisme) : neuf appels, chacun comparant l'exception (type et message) ou, pour le graphe retourné, l'isomorphisme et la conservation des liaisons de préfixes posées par l'original. Appels : path et baseuri None ; path http et baseuri (garde isUrl vraie, `URIRef(path)` et `URIRef(baseuri)`) ; path non-URL avec baseuri ; path https sans baseuri ; baseuri et path vides (`URIRef("")`, garde fausse) ; path entier ; graphe sans conteneur ; conteneur sans champ ; graph=None (exception de graph.query). Le graphe d'entrée porte un champ simple, des keywords avec entrées vides, un prédicat non mappé, un prédicat à espace final, un littéral vide, un littéral typé, un objet IRI et un second sujet qui n'est pas un conteneur.
mutants_killed: `rdflib.Graph(bind_namespaces="none")` dans la traduction (liaisons de l'original perdues)
garde `isUrl(path)` retirée (`path is not None` seul) ou inversée
keywords : strip, saut des entrées vides ou `continue` retirés
repair.remaining: Mutant équivalent : retirer `path is not None` de la garde reste vert (isUrl(None) est faux). Le shim `schemaOrg.distribution` rend le graphe tel quel (le dépôt n'a pas de méthode à trois arguments) : son effet réel n'est pas observé.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the unused `encodingFormats` list (and its comment) and the `mapping_data = []` initialisation go; the mapping index is one dict comprehension over `json.load(f)`; `container` is a conditional expression; `predUri = URIRef("http://schema.org/url")` is inlined as `so.url` and `URIRef("http://schema.org/" + ...)` becomes `so[...]`; the rows unpack as `pred, value`; `.keys()` goes; the keyword loop with its `continue`s becomes `schema_g += [... for kw in map(str.strip, value.split(',')) if kw]` and the trailing `continue` an `else`; `schema_org_inst` and the reassignment of `schema_g` become `return bald.schemaOrg().distribution(...)`. The file is opened before the query as in the original, so graph=None still raises the same AttributeError.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the SPARQL text becomes `s{ }` with `@prefix bald:` (still passed to `graph.query`, not `m{ }`: `m{ }(None)` would raise a different AttributeError message, which the driver compares); `Namespace` goes for `@prefix so:` + `@graph schema_g`; the type triple uses `a`; `URIRef(baseuri)` and `URIRef(path)` become `f<...>` (no @base in scope); `so[...]` becomes `so:{mapping_idx[currField]}`; the non-keyword add becomes `+{ {container} {predUri} {Literal(value)} }` (`Literal(...)` kept: an IRI value must become a literal, call 0). The keyword comprehension stays Python: one `+{ }` per keyword inside a loop and an `if` is longer. No exception to the symmetry rule.
The driver emits through harness._emit: rdfeval check proves every artefact.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: every import is used (rdflib.Graph, json, Namespace, BNode, URIRef, Literal, the two shim imports): a copy of optimized.py.
The driver emits through harness._emit: rdfeval check proves every artefact.
